page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) and 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, resulting in a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-quartile results in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests. However, the instance demonstrates average multi-core performance across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng multi-core suites. Notably, memory bandwidth for large-block read operations is strong, placing in the top 25%, while small-block reads and large-block writes remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5.16xlarge offers a standard resource density suitable for workloads requiring balanced compute and memory allocations without the premium of specialized hardware. Given its average multi-core capabilities and strong large-block memory read performance, it is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate Redis deployments. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, where its performance falls into the lower quartile.
